Standard: For all anticipated conditions, the electrical energy regenerated by actuators (e.g., by aerodynamic loading of the control surfaces or actuator reversal) is either stored or dissipated. Regenerated power characteristics are compatible with the energy storage systems or energy dissipation devices. There are no transients or reduction in performance when using stored power for actuation. A single failure in the storage system does not affect actuator performance. Subsystem thermal analysis accounts for heat produced by the actuators in both normal and failed conditions. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Actuator component-level test plans show that mission regeneration requirements are incorporated. Analysis.
  (1) Actuator regeneration supports mission requirements. Actuator duty cycle is developed by the analysis of all mission spectrums to generate worst-case loading and heating characteristics. Any usage assumptions and limitations resulting from the analysis are assessed and documented. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Supplier lab testing verifies regenerative power storage and dissipation meets mission requirements for all normal and required failure modes.
